native_result.query: How does the median wealth of white individuals compare to that of black and Hispanic individuals from 1985 onwards?
native_result.HypoA: 1985 onwards, white individuals have a significantly higher median wealth compared to black and Hispanic individuals.
native_result.HypoB: From 1985 onward, the median family net wealth of the white (non-Black/non-Hispanic) cohort is consistently and substantially higher than that of the black and Hispanic cohorts, and the racial wealth gap widens over time: in 1985 the white-proxy median ($3,500) was ~2.2x the black ($1,600) and ~7.0x the Hispanic ($500) median; by 1990 $12,972 (2.7x black, 8.1x Hispanic); and by 1996 $42,600 (4.4x black, 16.6x Hispanic), with the black cohort above the Hispanic cohort in every year. The ordering is robust to the 90th percentile, to dropping top-coded values, and to per-capita adjustment. Caveats: 'white' is a non-Black/non-Hispanic proxy (not strictly non-Hispanic white); wealth is family-level, not individual; values are nominal (not inflation-adjusted and not per-capita in the primary estimate), so the cross-year widening partly reflects inflation; and the 1996 estimates rest on a heavily attrited sample (~45% missing overall, 52.6% for the white-proxy group).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_raw.csv (12,686x61). For each year in {1985,1990,1996} and each racial/ethnic group {1=Black, 2=Hispanic, 3=White-proxy}, computed the median of family net wealth over non-missing values (listwise exclusion), reporting per-group n. Computed white/black and white/hispanic median ratios. Robustness: (a) 90th percentile per group/year; (b) median recomputed after dropping the top-coded repeated values (1,321,099 in 1990; 1,232,183 in 1996); (c) per-capita sensitivity (family net wealth / Family size, 1979). Also tabulated missingness/attrition by group and year. All checks preserve the white > black > hispanic ordering.
